Specifically, for any $f$, and for Lebesgue almost every $r$, the dimension of the level set satisfies:
$$ \dim f^{-1}(r) \ge s - \alpha $$
This is a deterministic lower bound derived from the fact that if the dimension were strictly less than $s-\alpha$, the function would need to vary "too slowly" or the set would be too sparse relative to the Hölder constraint, which contradicts the measure-theoretic properties of the map unless the function is constant on large scales (which generic functions are not).
